title: AI assistant for animators on Mac: voice help in Toon Boom, Blender and Photoshop
metaTitle: AI Assistant for Animators on Mac: Voice Help in 2026
description: An AI assistant for animators on Mac. Hold ⌥⌘, ask about your screen, and get spoken answers, pointers and draft notes in Harmony, Blender and Photoshop.
secondaryKeywords: AI assistant for animation on Mac
intro: An AI assistant for animators is a voice helper that reads your screen and answers while you work. Lazur is one for the Mac: hold ⌥⌘, ask a question, and it answers out loud, circles the control you need, or drafts the note you keep putting off. It works in Toon Boom Harmony, Blender, Photoshop and Chrome, but it does not click for you.
tldr: Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about anything on screen in Toon Boom Harmony, Blender or Photoshop.
It points at the control you need, or guides you one click at a time. It does not click for you.
Most animator admin is small and scattered. The real win is fewer detours out of the scene.
Check the macOS requirements for your app first. Blender 5.0 and later need Apple silicon.
Client files and unreleased footage follow your studio's rules before they follow any tool.

blocks.text: What an AI assistant for animators does on a Mac

Most animators do not need an AI that draws. You already draw. What you need is help with the work around the drawing: the menu you cannot find, the note to the director, the export setting you use once a month. An AI assistant for animators answers those small questions so you can stay in the file.

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It lives in the notch at the top of your screen. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask about anything you can see. Lazur answers out loud, and when you ask where something is, it draws a circle and a label around it. Hold fn to dictate clean text at the cursor in any app.

Lazur does not operate your apps. It does not click buttons, edit your file or move layers for you. You stay in charge of the work. That matters in animation, where one wrong click in a timeline can shift a whole shot.
Where an animator's day goes, and what the research says

The research on animators is thin. The studies I could open do not measure how animators split their hours between drawing, admin, email and menus. So the figures below come from nearby groups. Treat them as clues about your own week, not as a measurement of it.

A 2018 survey by The Creative Independent covered 1,016 visual artists. Of those, 42% spent five hours or fewer a week on admin, and 6% spent more than 25 hours. The average looks modest. The trouble is how the admin breaks up. A quick export question, a status email and a reference hunt land in the middle of a drawing session, and each one pulls you out of the scene.

Asana's Anatomy of Work Index says about six in ten work hours go to work about work rather than skilled work. The page covers more than 10,000 respondents, but it does not state its survey year, and it is not an animation study. Use it as a direction, not a precise figure.

Microsoft's 2023 Work Trend Index tells a similar story about email. The top 25% heaviest email users spend 8.8 hours a week on it. Those are top-quartile office workers on Microsoft 365, not averages, and not animators. They still show how fast an inbox fills a week.
Mac requirements for Toon Boom Harmony and Blender

Check the app before you ask an assistant for help inside it. Requirements change with each release, and older Intel Macs drop out faster than most people expect. Blender 4.5 LTS is the last release that supports Intel Macs, according to Blender's own requirements page.

blocks.title: Two Toon Boom pages list different Tahoe builds
blocks.text: Toon Boom's docs list macOS Tahoe as build 26.5.1 in one place. The product page lists 26.7.1. Open the requirements page yourself, then check your build under Apple menu > About This Mac before you update.
Adobe's Animate product page gives no version number and no macOS list. Check Adobe's own system requirements before you buy, and do not rely on a third-party summary.
How to ask Lazur for help without breaking your flow
The wording of your question decides what you get back. Ask for a location, a guide, a draft or a search. Each one maps to a different kind of help.

items: Ask where: 'Where is the PNG sequence export setting in Blender?' Lazur circles the control and labels it. You click.
Ask how: 'Walk me through a new layer in Photoshop.' Lazur guides you one click at a time and waits for each click.
Ask to write: 'Draft a reply that lists the three changes.' Lazur drafts the text, and you read it before you send.
Ask for research: 'Find the current minimum macOS version for Blender.' Lazur runs the search in its own Chrome tabs and reports back.

blocks.text: Avoid questions that ask for a result, such as 'Make the arc smoother.' That part is your job. Lazur can tell you where the smoothing control lives and explain what it does. It will not do the animation for you.
Frame by frame help in Photoshop, worked through

Say you open a PSD to tidy a walk cycle, and the frame timeline is hidden. You could search the menus. Or you could hold ⌥⌘ and ask. This is the small question that breaks a drawing session, and it takes seconds to answer when the answer is on screen.

Lazur sees the Photoshop window, so it knows which app is in front. It points at Window > Timeline and draws a circle around the menu item. Then you click, and Lazur waits. If you ask a follow-up, such as how to set a frame delay, it guides you through that step too.

Two mistakes come up often. First, ask for one panel or one setting at a time. A long question gets a long answer, and you lose your place. Second, check the result yourself. Lazur answers from what it sees, so a hidden panel or a cropped window can send it the wrong way.

For more on frame work, see [Photoshop for animators](/for/animators/photoshop). If the layer step is the one you need, the [steps to add a new layer in Photoshop](/how-to/add-a-new-layer-in-photoshop) show the menu path.
Revision notes and feedback without the admin pile-up

The Bureau of Labor Statistics describes part of an animator's job as editing animation based on feedback from directors or clients. The same job includes meeting clients and colleagues to review deadlines and timelines. Revisions are where the admin piles up.

CGWire says two rounds of revisions on a commercial project might be expected. Five rounds is a sign something broke down earlier. Those are rules of thumb with no measured hours behind them, so use them to judge your own project and your own client.

items: Hold fn and dictate the director's note as you hear it, word for word.
Ask Lazur to draft a reply that restates each change and asks one question.
Read the draft out loud. Cut anything you would not say to the client.
Paste it into your email or tracker yourself, then send it.

blocks.text: Privacy, client files and your studio's rules

Lazur listens and looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Those statements describe what happens on the Lazur side only.

blocks.title: Check your studio's rules first
blocks.text: Unreleased footage, client scripts and pre-release character designs can be confidential. Follow your studio's rules and your client contract before you ask any AI tool about them. Lazur's privacy notes do not replace either one.

If you work from home with a client's files open, close the windows you do not need before you hold the shortcut. Lazur sees what is on your screen, so a private folder in the corner of the display is in view too.
Mistakes animators make with an AI assistant

items: Letting go too early. Lazur listens only while you hold ⌥⌘ or fn, so keep holding until the whole question is out.
Trusting a menu path without checking the version. Menus move between releases. Check the app's About box and your Mac under Apple menu > About This Mac.
Dictating into the wrong field. Dictation types at the cursor, so click into the right box before you hold fn.
Expecting Lazur to click. It will not press the button. It waits while you do.
Asking one giant question. Split it into short ones. Short questions get short answers you can check.

blocks.text: Research and browser work in Chrome

Animators check references, plugin pages and render documentation in a browser. That work tends to scatter across tabs. Lazur for Chrome lets Lazur run research in its own Chrome tabs. It comes back with a summary and a report, so your own tabs stay where you left them.
Ask something like 'Find the current macOS requirement for Blender 5.0.' Lazur checks the vendor's page and reports back. For more browser help, see [Chrome for animators](/for/animators/chrome).
What Lazur costs and how to start

Lazur starts with a 3-day Pro trial. No credit card is needed, and the trial starts the first time you open the app. Pro costs $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually, with 250 AI actions. Power costs $120 a month, or $96 a month annually, with 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both plans.
Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available. Get the app from the [download page](/download), and check [pricing](/pricing) before you pick a plan.

blocks.title: A fair test
blocks.text: Use the trial on a shot you have already finished. You will see quickly whether the help saves you searches, or just adds another window to watch.
What to do next

items: Pick the app you open most, whether that is Toon Boom Harmony, Blender or Photoshop.
Check its macOS requirements against the table above, then check your own build.
Install Lazur from the download page and start the trial on a finished shot.
Write down the questions you ask twice a week. Those are your best candidates for voice help.
Read your studio's rules on client files before you share anything with an AI tool.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Toon Boom Harmony and Blender?
faq.answer: Lazur sees your screen in any app on your Mac, so it can point at controls in Toon Boom Harmony, Blender or Photoshop. It is not a plugin or add-in for any of them, and no app maker has partnered with Lazur. Check each app's requirements page before you install anything.

faq.question: Does Lazur draw, edit or click for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate other apps for you. It points, guides you one step at a time, answers out loud and drafts text. You do the drawing and the clicking.

faq.question: Is there a Windows version?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

faq.question: When does Lazur listen and look at my screen?
faq.answer: Only while you hold the shortcut. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about the screen, or hold fn to dictate. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: What does Lazur cost?
faq.answer: There is a 3-day Pro trial with no credit card. Pro is $18 a month, or $15 a month billed annually, with 250 AI actions. Power is $120 a month, or $96 a month annually, with 1,000 AI actions. Dictation is unlimited on both. See the pricing page for current terms.

faq.question: Can Lazur run research while I keep working?
faq.answer: Yes. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension, and it comes back with a summary and a report. Your own tabs stay yours.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur with client files?
faq.answer: Follow your studio's rules and your client contract first. Lazur sends what it sees to AI providers to answer, so treat confidential footage or scripts with the same care you would give any outside tool.

faq.question: Does Lazur remember my earlier questions?
faq.answer: Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did. That memory is kept on your Mac.

painPoints.title: Work about work takes most of the hours
painPoints.text: Asana says about six in ten work hours go to work about work. That is a general figure, not an animation one, and the page does not state its survey year.

painPoints.text: BLS says animators edit work based on feedback from directors or clients, and meet to review deadlines. CGWire says two revision rounds is normal and five means something broke earlier.

painPoints.title: Self-employed means you run the admin too
painPoints.text: BLS reports 63% of special effects artists and animators were self-employed. If you invoice, schedule and send status notes, that time sits with you.

painPoints.title: Email fills the week
painPoints.text: Microsoft's top 25% heaviest email users spend 8.8 hours a week on email. Those are office workers, but the numbers show how fast an inbox fills a week.

painPoints.title: Every how-to question pulls you off the canvas
painPoints.text: Looking up a menu, a shortcut or a setting means leaving the file. Each detour costs attention, and no study I opened measures how much.
